verdict.rationale: Navan documents an official MCP server for querying spend data, including flagged expenses and policy violations. It also offers an OAuth API with retrieval and update endpoints for card transactions and manual expenses, plus custom-field and batch option-value management. Together these let an agent pull transactions, reason about categorization and policy, and write coding back. Missing for 10: an explicit filter or state for 'uncoded' transactions, documented write or update actions via MCP (MCP appears query-oriented), a documented review/staging step for agent-proposed coding, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
